prompt: A conjugated enone (α,β-unsaturated ketone) shows its C=O IR band at ~1680 cm⁻¹, LOWER than a non-conjugated ketone (~1715). Why?

options.label: Conjugation delocalizes the C=O π electrons, lowering the bond's force constant and its stretching frequency
The adjacent C=C adds mass to the oscillator, increasing reduced mass and lowering ν
Conjugation reduces the C=O dipole moment, which couples to a lower IR absorption frequency
The α-carbon is sp² in the enone, which pulls the C=O frequency down by hybridization

explanation: Conjugation delocalizes π electrons from the C=O into the C=C, giving the C=O partial single-bond character. Weaker effective bond → lower force constant → lower stretching frequency (by ~30 cm⁻¹). Reduced mass and dipole moment don't drive the shift — bond strength does.
